key_insight: Librarian Agents train an LLM to proactively reorganize raw documents into a reusable workspace, so future questions can be answered more accurately and efficiently than with reactive retrieval.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new design pattern for long-context systems: build anticipatory, task-agnostic workspaces offline, then reuse them across downstream queries to reduce inference-time bottlenecks.
method: Builder agent converts unstructured corpora into a hierarchical filesystem of synthetic files and reference links.
Workspace construction is formulated as a Markov decision process.
A reinforcement-learning objective directly optimizes the builder for downstream answering accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 33-point gain over strong retrieval and precomputation baselines on BrowseComp-Plus and a 31-point average accuracy improvement zero-shot on BRIGHT.
watch_item: The approach adds upfront construction cost and complexity, so practical value depends on whether queries are repeated enough to amortize workspace building and whether the synthetic structure remains robust across domains.
paper_title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
